fr.draining_pipes.text: high confidence: Asks about rainwater or stormwater pipes instead of pipes carrying polluted water, so a clean storm drain outlet counts as yes in French but not in English.
fr.construction.text: high confidence: Widens the scope from works in the stream to works in or around it, so building work on a nearby road or bank top counts as yes in French but not in English.

it.draining_pipes.text: high confidence: Asks about rainwater instead of polluted water, so any rain drain outlet counts as yes in Italian while English asks only about pipes carrying polluted water.
it.bank_type.text: medium confidence: "Banchi" is a false friend: in Italian it means shoals or bars (as in "banchi di sabbia", the sand banks option) or benches, not the river banks, so the volunteer may describe deposits in the channel instead of its banks.
it.habitats.option:riffles: medium confidence: "Ruscellamenti" means surface runoff over land, not riffles in the stream (Italian "raschi"), so the first habitat named is a different thing.

nl.habitats.option:riffles: medium confidence: "Geultjes" means small gullies or channels, not riffles (shallow fast water over gravel), so a volunteer may tick this for small side channels and may not tick it for a riffle.
nl.sewage_discharge.text: medium confidence: Narrows the question to sewage only and joins the two cases with "and" instead of "or"; "afvoer" can also read as sewage being carried away (a sewer), so a volunteer who sees only a clean inflow, or only a sewage outfall, may answer no.

no.habitats.option:riffles: medium confidence: "Strømvirvler" means eddies or whirlpools, which are slow swirling water, not riffles (shallow fast broken water), so the first habitat named is a different one.
no.vegetation_type_left.option:herbs: medium confidence: "Ugress" means weeds (unwanted plants), not herbs or herbaceous plants as a growth form, so a margin of grasses and wild herbs may not be seen as matching.
no.vegetation_type_right.option:herbs: medium confidence: "Ugress" means weeds (unwanted plants), not herbs or herbaceous plants as a growth form, so a margin of grasses and wild herbs may not be seen as matching.
no.feelings.option:anger: medium confidence: "Raseri" means rage or fury, much stronger than anger (Norwegian "sinne"), so a volunteer who feels angry or annoyed but not furious is less likely to pick it.

pt.vegetation_type_left.text: medium confidence: Drops "from the channel banktop", so the 5 m strip has no stated starting point and will most likely be counted from the water edge, which on a deep channel includes the bank slope instead of the strip beyond the banktop.
pt.vegetation_type_right.text: medium confidence: Drops "from the channel bank/top", so the 5 m strip has no stated starting point and will most likely be counted from the water edge, which on a deep channel includes the bank slope instead of the strip beyond the banktop.
pt.sewage_discharge.text: medium confidence: Narrows the question to sewage only; the English (and the fr, it and no versions) also asks about any kind of water entry, so a clean inflow such as a side stream or drain counts as yes in English but not in Portuguese. The English sentence is itself ambiguous, so this may reflect the original intent.
